problem: Offer storage as a service with no minimum fee.
title: Amazon launches S3 pay-as-you-go storage for developers
context: Developers had to buy and run their own storage infrastructure.
decision_made: Launch Amazon S3 at $0.15 per gigabyte per month plus $0.20 per gigabyte transferred.
action_taken: Announced in a March 2006 press release with an application programming interface.
observed_outcome: AWS reported twenty years later that the service still runs and that storage prices fell by roughly 85 percent since launch.
lessons: Selling infrastructure as a metered service can create a durable platform, with prices falling as scale grows.
limitations: Self-reported by AWS. Sources give 13 or 14 March as the date. Revenue and share figures were not found.

claims.claim_text: AWS launched S3 at $0.15 per GB per month and $0.20 per GB transferred, with no minimum fee.
AWS says its storage price is down about 85 percent since the 2006 launch.
